evidence: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym. config/site_settings.yml:59-62 gives default_locale a default of 'en' and enum LocaleSiteSetting, so the enum only allows valid locale strings and the value is never nil. app/controllers/application_controller.rb:156 already uses SiteSetting.default_locale unguarded. Adding &. would not help anyway: if the value were nil, `.compact` would drop it and the fallback chain would silently skip the site locale.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:5 uses I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Pluralization). This line was moved unchanged from the deleted config/initializers/pluralization.rb:2. The codebase uses the same idiom elsewhere (config/initializers/strong_parameters.rb:1, lib/discourse_plugin.rb:23). It is true that Module#include is public since Ruby 2.1, but the two forms behave the same, so this is cosmetic.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:9 uses I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks). Direct include behaves the same on Ruby 2.1+, and send(:include) is the idiom already used in this codebase (config/initializers/strong_parameters.rb:1, lib/discourse_plugin.rb:23). This is a cosmetic change only.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:21 was not changed by this PR, so the comment is out of scope. It is also wrong on the merits: lines 23-33 override handle_unverified_request on purpose. The override calls super (which resets the session), clears current_user and renders a 403 'BAD CSRF' response, with an exemption for API-key requests. Using `with: :exception` would bypass this handler and break the API-key exemption and the custom 403 response.
